concepts.def: Processes instructions via the fetch–decode–execute cycle.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Computer Architecture — a core area of A-Level Computer Science.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Computer Architecture brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Computer Architecture.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

What is the main advantage of asymmetric encryption?
options: It is impossible to break.
To make the database look neater.
It is faster than symmetric encryption.
Secure key exchange without sharing a secret in advance.

mcqs.q: What is the purpose of database normalisation?
options: It is impossible to break.
To make the database look neater.
To reduce redundancy and avoid update anomalies.
To make the database run faster.

mcqs.q: What does it mean that RAM is volatile?
options: Its contents are lost when power is removed.
It can explode or be damaged easily.
It is impossible to break.
It can store data permanently.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “CPU components”?
options: Manages CPU scheduling, memory, file systems, I/O, security; UNIX 1969 (Thompson & Ritchie).
Primary (RAM, cache) volatile, fast; secondary (HDD, SSD) non-volatile, slower, larger.
Base-2 numerals; integers as two's complement; characters via ASCII (1963) or Unicode UTF-8.
Arithmetic Logic Unit, Control Unit, registers (MAR, MDR, PC, IR, accumulator); fetch-decode-execute cycle.
